dropped.7: `agent({ system })` is gone; the field is `systemPrompt`. The alias existed to match the Vercel AI SDK's spelling and made `agent({ system, systemPrompt })` representable, which then needed a runtime throw to forbid — one concept with two names and a rule to police them. A stale `system` is reported by name, because it is in the stray-field renames map.
dropped.8: Pre-release: `StaticAgentParams` is now `Omit<StaticAgentParamsCore, WorkflowAppOnlyField>` plus the misuse messages, rather than sharing a third unexported base with the arm — so this epoch would in fact still compile, the shape being identical. Dropped rather than retained because the SDK has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty. The change exists so the docs build has one name to resolve instead of two: TypeDoc refuses an undocumented type on a public signature, and `StaticAgentParamsBase` was a second one.

dropped.10: Collateral: this capability's report names ToolContext.workflows / WorkflowClient, so WorkflowCtx's two new methods reach it. The change is the DevKit removal's phases 2 and 3, not this surface.
dropped.11: Collateral: this capability's report names ToolContext.workflows / WorkflowClient, so WorkflowCtx's waitFor overload reaches it.
dropped.12: `WorkflowCtx.step`'s `name` narrowed from `string` to `Name & Literal<Name>`, so a name that has widened to `string` — exactly the shape that re-executes a step on replay — is now a compile error rather than a runtime surprise. Epoch N authoring code that built a step name at runtime therefore does not compile, which is the point of the change; and this package has no external consumer to keep an epoch-N template for.

dropped.14: ctx.sleep takes a label as its first argument: a wait is keyed sleep!<label>#<occurrence> rather than positionally, so a body reaching a different number of waits no longer reads another wait's record. WorkflowCtx is reachable from this capability's report.
dropped.15: Collateral: this report names ToolContext.workflows, whose WorkflowDef/WorkflowCtx parameter types moved. Additive: the schema options and WorkflowDef.output are all optional, so the superseded epoch would in fact still compile. Dropped rather than retained because the SDK has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty, matching every prior epoch entry here.

dropped.1: `webSearch` takes ONE name for its cap, in ONE position: `maxResults`, in the options bag. It used to accept `max_results` too — the only snake_case identifier on this SDK's TypeScript surface — and `maxResults` again in the second parameter, so one option had three ways to arrive and two were undiscoverable from the third. `max_results` remains the WIRE name the model-facing builtin schema declares; only the TypeScript helper narrowed.
dropped.2: An untyped fetchJson/webSearch/visitWebpage no longer answers `any`, so an epoch-2 caller reading a field off an unnarrowed result stops compiling — which is the defect: the T | ToolFailure union was collapsing to any. Same class as epoch 1's drop. CallOptions also gained an optional signal, which is additive.

Dropped rather than retained on the same grounds as `aai-runtime:db` epoch 1: there is no external consumer to keep an epoch-1 template for, and no `uploads` example exists to extend, so a retain would oblige a frozen fixture exercising all eight names to evidence a compatibility nobody is relying on.

Pre-release: StandardSchemaIssue gains an OPTIONAL `errors` field (a vendor extension formatSchemaIssues reads for union branches), so this epoch would in fact still compile — dropped rather than retained because the SDK has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty.
dropped.2: A workflow body is now (input, ctx) and carries no compiler-stamped workflowId: the Workflow DevKit's "use workflow"/"use step" directives are replaced by ctx.step, so a body written at epoch 2 does not compile.
dropped.3: ctx.sleep and ctx.waitFor were added to WorkflowCtx: durable suspension (phase 2) and hooks (phase 3) of the DevKit removal. A body written at the previous epoch still compiles, but the engine it was written for did not have either, so the epoch evidences nothing.
dropped.4: ctx.waitFor gained a timeout option, so a hook's deadline is a parameter rather than a Promise.race against ctx.sleep — both suspend, and a suspend unwinds the stack, so the race stops the body before the other side is reached.
dropped.5: isWorkflowSuspend is new, and it is part of the authoring surface rather than an engine internal: a catch inside a body must re-throw the engine's suspend signal or its failure path runs against a run that was only waiting. recap-workflow shipped that bug.
dropped.6: `WorkflowCtx.step`'s `name` narrowed from `string` to `Name & Literal<Name>`, so a name that has widened to `string` — exactly the shape that re-executes a step on replay — is now a compile error rather than a runtime surprise. Epoch N authoring code that built a step name at runtime therefore does not compile, which is the point of the change; and this package has no external consumer to keep an epoch-N template for.
dropped.7: WorkflowCtx gains now()/random()/uuid() — three journaled non-deterministic reads — so this epoch would in fact still compile: a workflow BODY only ever receives that type. Dropped rather than retained because the SDK has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty.
dropped.8: isWorkflowSuspend is REMOVED, because a suspension can no longer reach a workflow body at all. ctx.sleep and ctx.waitFor used to suspend by THROWING a branded signal, so a body's catch had to test it and re-throw — advice, which one shipped template forgot, deleting the transcript its run was waiting for. A wait now returns a promise that never settles and the engine races the body against an out-of-band interruption channel, so there is nothing for a catch to catch and nothing left for an author to remember. A body written at epoch 8 that named the predicate does not compile.
dropped.9: ctx.sleep takes a label as its first argument: a wait is keyed sleep!<label>#<occurrence> rather than positionally, so a body reaching a different number of waits no longer reads another wait's record. WorkflowCtx is reachable from this capability's report.
dropped.10: ctx.step and ctx.waitFor gained an optional `schema`, and WorkflowDef gained an optional `output` (with WorkflowOutputOf reading it). Additive: the schema options and WorkflowDef.output are all optional, so the superseded epoch would in fact still compile. Dropped rather than retained because the SDK has no external consumers and contracts/compatibility/ stays empty, matching every prior epoch entry here.
